correctness.rationale: On an intrinsic Euclidean cone disk, radial area density 2r/R² and uniform shorter angular difference δ on [0,x] (x=α/2) combine with d²=r²+s²-2rs cos(min(δ,π)). Using E r²=R²/2 and E(rs)=4R²/9 gives F(x)=(9x-8sin x)/(9x²) to π and (17x-8π)/(9x²) above π, with apex-geodesic probability 1-π/x only for x>π. For the ordinary cone branch the derivative numerator G=16sin x-x(9+8cos x), G''=8xcos x, and endpoint signs prove exactly two roots x_-≈0.925373 and x_+≈2.922168 and one global minimum at x_-; the upper root is a local maximum. The exact F(7π/8)>F(π) gives three solutions for levels in (1/π,F(x_+)). For x>π, F'<0. Expansion about π verifies F is C² not C³ with third derivative jump -8/(9π²). The analytic derivation, not the finite Monte Carlo checker read in full, proves all parameter claims.
